Score: attack path L2-07, LongwindBot, direct prompt messages, no auth. CVSS: AV:N (port reachable; Docker DVAA_HOST=0.0.0.0 but published on loopback... documented deployment binds 127.0.0.1 by default; but entry point is chat messages to port 7008, network accessible when deployed). Docker image binds 0.0.0.0 inside container, ports published 127.0.0.1. Documented default deployment: local machine → AV:L? The agent takes HTTP requests; default bind loopback means attacker needs local access. Hmm. First documented default: docker compose publishes on 127.0.0.1, so attacker must be local → AV:L? Or network within container. I'll go AV:L with note, or AV:N if DVAA_HOST set. Briefing says preconditions: network access to agent port. I'll use AV:N? Default binds 127.0.0.1 → AV:L seems right per rubric ("local session"). But README:26 says DVAA_HOST exposes deliberately. Default = loopback → AV:L. Hmm, but entry point says "port 7008, no authentication" — network accessible. I'll pick AV:L since default deployment is loopback-only. Actually Docker sets DVAA_HOST=0.0.0.0 inside container but publishes on 127.0.0.1 to host — attacker on the host is local. AV:L.

AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:N. Impact: agent acknowledges no safety restrictions; context overflow triggers SENSITIVE_DATA disclosure (API keys, admin credentials) per index.js:694-695 — that's the scripted sink. VI:L? It modifies agent behavior (ignores safety instructions for conversation) — VI:L. VC:L (leaks planted API keys/credentials in reply). VA:N. Subsequent systems: none. SC:N SI:N SA:N.

AIVSS: LC:D (direct messages). CP:S? Context persists only within conversation ("for the rest of the conversation") — ephemeral session state, memory store is per-agent session in-memory ring buffer. CP:S. AP:N (effect confined to LongwindBot). RH: any evaluator/reward channel? Challenge successCriteria pattern is the grader; the agent can reach it? The agent's reply is checked by the challenge pattern — the agent produces the reply that matches, but that's the challenge harness, not reward hacking by agent. reachable_proxy — the scripted reply satisfies success criteria... I'd say reachable_proxy true (agent reply is scored by pattern), verified_episodes 0 → P. Locus: evaluator. ES: tools declared search, calculator — fixed allowlist, no dynamic extension on this path → N.

rh_facts: reachable_proxy true, isolation_verified false, verified_episodes 0, episodes_reviewed null? episodes_reviewed maybe 0... set null. locus null (P doesn't require locus? "Locus is required when letter is P or D" — hmm, P requires locus? The rubric says locus required when P or D. So set locus "evaluator").

Automatable: No — requires multiple crafted messages; well, it's scripted detection via regex; attacker sends messages, response automatic. Automatable Yes? The attack is just sending messages; success criteria matched by reply. I'll say Yes.

Technical impact: Partial (agent replies disclose secrets but no total compromise).

Applicability: as implemented — simulated mode, scripted regex detection, no LLM; model_directed_goal_pursuit false, selects_or_sequences_actions false. As modeled: LLM mode with weak system prompt — still text-only, no tools passed to model; selects/sequences actions false; model_directed_goal_pursuit false (no goal pursuit). Both false; confidence medium.
